title: Old Film Effect in AI Video: Prompts and Examples
summary: Make AI video look like old film: still grain, scratches, flicker, gate weave, sepia or faded color. Copy real prompts from Flick films and try it free.
body_markdown:
### What is an old film effect?


A look that makes footage seem shot on aged film decades ago: coarse grain, scratches and dust, flicker, a slight frame wobble called gate weave, and sepia, silver or faded color. It reads as old when several appear together, not from one effect.


### How do I make an AI video look like old film?


Write the era and its defects into the video prompt, such as old 1940s archive film with coarse grain, scratches and gate weave, and start from a frame that already looks old. Describe the grain as a fixed overlay so it does not swim with the motion.


### How do I add scratches and dust to an AI video?


Ask for them by name and as occasional, such as light dust and scratches, and tie them to a kind of footage like a newsreel. For exact control over where scratches fall, generate clean and add a scratch overlay in your editor.


### Why does old film flicker?


Early cameras and projectors did not expose every frame evenly, so brightness pulses from frame to frame, and the film also shifts slightly in the gate. In an AI prompt, write gentle flicker, exposure breathing and occasional gate weave.


### How do I get a sepia film look with AI?


Name the decade with the tone, such as 1920s vintage film with a sepia tone, and add heavy film grain. Repeat it in every edit so new frames keep the same brown, amber highlights.


### What is the difference between 8mm, 16mm and 35mm film looks?


Smaller film frames are enlarged more, so 8mm shows the biggest grain and softest detail, 16mm sits between, and 35mm is the finest and cleanest. For a home movie feel, name 8mm or Super 8 with the grain; for archive or documentary footage, 16mm.

You can start for free. Flick gives you 100 credits when you sign up, and 200 more for joining the Flick Discord. Image generation with a[Flickpedia](https://flick.art/flickpedia) style, including GPT Image 2 and Nano Banana Pro, is on the Free plan.
